cards.text: God has a message for Israel, the people He chose as His own (Deuteronomy 7:6), and it comes through a man named Malachi. Being chosen? I KNOW that feeling. Somebody picked me out of a clearance bin for 25 cents, and I still haven't gotten over it.

cards.question: Here come the LORD's first words to Israel through Malachi. What does He tell them?
Israel hears the LORD say “I have loved you” and takes it right in, no questions asked.

cards.text: Nope. Israel fires right back: “How have You loved us?” That's like telling somebody “I love you” and they look up from their phone and go, “Okay. Send me the receipts.”
So the LORD answers with a question of His own: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” Esau and Jacob were twin sons of Isaac (Genesis 25:24-26), and later God renamed Jacob as Israel (Genesis 35:10).

cards.question: The LORD is talking to Israel, the people who came from Jacob. Which one does He say He has loved?

cards.text: Jacob. Then the LORD says, “but Esau I have hated,” and He points to what's become of Esau's land.

cards.question: The LORD says He has made Esau's mountains a ___ and left his inheritance to the desert jackals.

cards.text: Edom, Esau's people (Genesis 36:1), may say, “We have been devastated, but we will rebuild the ruins,” and honestly, I respect that. When MY edges wore down, I got slid into the back of a junk drawer and didn't even TRY to climb out.

cards.question: Edom plans to rebuild the ruins. What does the LORD of Hosts say about that?

answers.text: He will tear down what they build
He will help them build it back
He will let them build in peace

cards.question: The LORD says He will be indignant with Edom for only a little while.

cards.text: Forever, and Edom will be called the Land of Wickedness. “You will see this with your own eyes,” the LORD tells Israel.

cards.question: Israel will see all this for themselves. What does the LORD say they will end up saying about Him?

answers.text: He is great even beyond Israel
He is great only inside Israel
He has stepped away from Israel

cards.text: That's it, they'll say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.” My greatness? It stops at the edge of one little cookie planet, and the OVEN gets most of the credit.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'God has a message for Israel… Malachi.' / 'Being chosen?' / 'I KNOW that feeling.' / 'Somebody picked me out… gotten over it.' The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Malachi 1:1 calls it 'the burden of the word of the LORD,' but the card calls it 'a message.' That swaps out the text's own term and drops its weight. The card should keep 'burden' (the dictionary pop-up can explain it), for example: 'The LORD has a burden, a word for Israel, and it comes through a man named Malachi.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Nope.' / 'Israel fires right back: “How have You loved us?”' / 'That's like telling somebody…' Story cards after the opening card are limited to two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Jacob.', which confirms the card 6 answer from Malachi 1:2, but it cites only Malachi 1:3. Other cards that confirm an answer include that verse in their range (card 12 cites 1:4-5). This card should cite Malachi 1:2-3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card says 'Edom, Esau's people (Genesis 36:1).' Genesis 36:1 says Esau himself is Edom ('Esau (that is, Edom)'). It doesn't call Edom Esau's people. A verse that states the fact, such as Genesis 36:9 ('Esau, the father of the Edomites'), should be cited instead.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'That's it, they'll say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.”' / 'My greatness?' / 'It stops at the edge… most of the credit.' Story cards after the opening card are limited to two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
